Assembled 2026-10-25 from proofread BSB page files 00089-00099 at repository revision 176a2557: 203 measures, 11 surfaces and 43 systems. BuxWV 259 identity follows the existing corpus work index; staff roles follow the five-staff page encodings. Correction credits follow page-file history for Francy Häring, Jan-Raphael Kemnitzer and Egor Polyakov. DdT 1903 is the documented base source. Selective comparison with the Uppsala Op. II print through STIMU 1991 supports the gamba E4 dotted whole at m. 114 (2026-10-25; Viola da Gamba, Sonata I, Grave, printed p. 4, fifth staff; scan-0027, left page) and the gamba E-natural4 at m. 24, beat 2 (2026-11-03; staff 6; scan-0026, left page). Source-supported annotations and supplemental excerpts document these readings; no complete historical-print collation is claimed. Assembly preserved the musical readings, clefs and meters; subsequent editor-confirmed corrections are recorded in the MEI revision history. The m. 90 upper-keyboard lower-voice F4 is a documented conjectural eighth on the final eighth-note subdivision, departing from its apparent quarter-note form in DdT. At m. 163 the opening upper-keyboard A-flat4 is a documented conjectural dotted quarter, restoring 6/4 and the beat-3 alignment where DdT appears undotted. Inherited MusicXML ppq and dur.ppq were stripped on 2026-10-25 following the notebook workflow and the other assembled scores. Work-level correction was completed with Egor Polyakov in the 2026-10-25–26 editing session; the editor confirmed corrected status on 2026-10-26. Remaining report warnings do not imply uncorrected musical text; final publication sign-off remains separate.

This file contains only the four-dance suite component of BuxWV 273, printed in DdT as Appendix I to Op. I/4; it is not the complete BuxWV 273 sonata with suite. Catalogue identification checked against Edition Guentersberg G126 (https://www.guentersberg.de/noten/de/g126.php). The editor confirmed on 2026-10-20 that DdT 1903 was the only source consulted for this suite up to that date. Uppsala University Library, Imhs 13:25 (Düben Collection Database Catalogue, source 2089), was identified on 2026-11-06 and has been examined selectively: its dances were located, and measure 83 was read in the Organo and Viola de Gamba parts. It has not been collated. Five staff roles checked against DdT and encoded definitions. Credits follow assembled-file history for Jingyu Tu and Egor Polyakov.

Catalogue identity checked against Edition Guentersberg G133 (https://www.guentersberg.de/noten/de/g133.php). Six staff roles checked against DdT. Credits follow assembled-file history for Lea Meret Beck and Egor Polyakov. DdT is the documented correction basis. The editor suggested STIMU for a placeholder annotation, but its pointer belongs to Op. II/6, m. 3, and provides no historical-source evidence for this appendix. A targeted digital examination of Uppsala manuscript Instr. mus. i hskr. 13:27, source 2090, violin II, was begun on 2026-10-20; the m. 156 reading was confirmed by selective examination on 2026-11-06. No full collation or exclusive earlier source history is claimed. On 2026-10-20 the editor approved the inferred subsidiary-voice allocation at m. 34 and the conjectural C4 dot at m. 70. On the review page of 2026-11-06 the editor adopted the manuscript’s D5 eighth followed by an eighth rest at m. 156, replacing the interim conjecture that kept a D5 quarter and omitted that rest. Claude read the manuscript at full resolution. The source record links all four parts: Violino 1mo, Violino 2do, Viola di gamba and Continuo. The additional source pass corrected the gamba tenor-clef passage at mm. 28–40, the pitches misread a third high at mm. 28–31, and the keyboard B4 at m. 34; later C-clefs were checked individually. The editor subsequently approved a conjectural dot on the opening E4 at m. 70 as well; its following alignment space is removed without shifting later notes. The separate m. 28 clef annotation is removed because the repaired encoding follows DdT; the correction remains in revision history.
